I will keep my land in the wheat-maize rotation this year. In Quzhou, this is the crop pattern I trust most because the land, weather, and my experience all fit it. By mid-April, the winter wheat is already in the ground, so I will carry that crop through harvest, then I will go straight into summer maize on the same fields. I will not spread myself across too many crops. Cotton and peanuts can make sense some years, but they need more judgment on timing and management, and I would rather stay with the crops I know best and that give me steady grain and income. I will keep fertilizer moderate instead of pushing too hard, because water is always a constraint here and I do not want to waste money or burn the crop. I will irrigate wheat twice if needed and maize once if the summer rain is short. I will use improved wheat seed and hybrid maize seed because I want reliable emergence and stable yield. For tillage, I will use rotary tillage before wheat and no-tillage for maize after wheat harvest so I can save time and keep moisture.
